commands.howToUse: Provide the repo URL followed by your desired folder name.
commands.whenToUse: When organizing multiple projects or avoiding naming conflicts.
commands.tip: Useful for keeping your workspace clean and structured.

commands.title: Shallow clone (fast)
commands.description: Clones only the latest snapshot of a repository without full history.
commands.howToUse: Add --depth 1 before the repository URL when cloning.
commands.whenToUse: When you only need the latest code and want faster downloads on mobile.
commands.tip: Great for saving data and storage on Termux environments.

commands.title: Clone a specific branch
commands.description: Clones only one specified branch instead of the entire repository.
commands.howToUse: Replace 'develop' with the target branch name and run the command.
commands.whenToUse: When working only on a feature or staging branch.
commands.tip: Reduces download size by avoiding unnecessary branches.

commands.title: Fork + clone workflow
commands.code: git clone git@github.com:YOUR-USERNAME/repo.git && cd repo && git remote add upstream git@github.com:ORIGINAL-OWNER/repo.git
commands.description: Sets up a forked repository with upstream tracking for syncing changes.
commands.howToUse: Fork the repo on GitHub, clone your fork, then add upstream remote.
commands.whenToUse: When contributing to open-source projects via pull requests.
commands.tip: Always sync upstream regularly to avoid merge conflicts.

commands.title: Init + update submodules
commands.description: Initializes and updates all submodules in a repository.
commands.howToUse: Run after cloning a repo that contains submodules.
commands.whenToUse: When a project depends on external Git repositories.
commands.tip: Always run this after fresh clone to avoid missing dependencies.

commands.title: Clone a repository
commands.description: Creates a full local copy of a remote repository.
commands.howToUse: Replace user/repo with the actual GitHub repository path and run inside your projects directory.
commands.whenToUse: When starting work on any existing GitHub project.
commands.tip: Prefer SSH for smoother authentication if configured.

commands.title: Clone into a custom folder
commands.description: Clones a repository into a user-defined folder name.
commands.howToUse: Add a folder name after the repo URL.
commands.whenToUse: When organizing multiple projects locally.
commands.tip: Helps avoid cluttered default repo folder names.

commands.title: Clone a specific branch
commands.description: Clones only a selected branch instead of the full repository.
commands.howToUse: Replace 'develop' with your desired branch name.
commands.whenToUse: When focusing on a single feature or environment branch.
commands.tip: Useful for lightweight development setups.

commands.title: Show branch tracking info
commands.description: Displays local branches and their upstream tracking status.
commands.howToUse: Run inside any Git repository.
commands.whenToUse: When checking sync status with remote branches.
commands.tip: Helps identify branches that need push or pull updates.

commands.title: Show current branch
commands.description: Displays the currently active Git branch.
commands.howToUse: Run in any repository to instantly see your active branch.
commands.whenToUse: Before committing or pushing changes.
commands.tip: Prevents accidental commits to wrong branches.

commands.title: Show remote details
commands.description: Displays detailed information about the remote repository configuration.
commands.howToUse: Run inside the repository to inspect remote setup.
commands.whenToUse: When debugging remote connection issues.
commands.tip: Useful for verifying upstream tracking branches.

commands.title: Show remote branches
commands.description: Lists all branches available on the remote repository.
commands.howToUse: Run inside repository with remote configured.
commands.whenToUse: When checking available branches on GitHub.
commands.tip: Does not fetch branches locally.

commands.title: Show changed filenames
commands.description: Shows only filenames that have been modified.
commands.howToUse: Run inside repository before committing.
commands.whenToUse: When reviewing what files changed quickly.
commands.tip: Faster alternative to full diff output.

commands.title: Show staged filenames
commands.description: Lists files currently staged for commit.
commands.howToUse: Run after staging files with git add.
commands.whenToUse: Before committing to verify staged changes.
commands.tip: Prevents accidental commits of unwanted files.

commands.title: Show files changed between branches
commands.description: Displays files that differ between two branches.
commands.howToUse: Replace branch names and run inside repository.
commands.whenToUse: Before merging branches or opening a PR.
commands.tip: Helps identify impact of changes before merge.

commands.title: Restore file from another branch
commands.description: Restores a file from another branch into the current branch.
commands.howToUse: Specify source branch and file path.
commands.whenToUse: When recovering or copying file versions across branches.
commands.tip: Useful for selective file recovery.

commands.title: Restore file from a commit
commands.description: Restores a file from a specific commit.
commands.howToUse: Replace commit hash and file path.
commands.whenToUse: When recovering an older version of a file.
commands.tip: Does not affect other project files.

commands.title: Create branch from stash
commands.description: Creates a new branch and applies a stash to it.
commands.howToUse: Run with stash reference to restore work safely.
commands.whenToUse: When continuing stashed work in isolation.
commands.tip: Safest way to recover complex stashed changes.

commands.title: Stash a single file
commands.description: Stashes changes from a single file only.
commands.howToUse: Specify the file path to stash individually.
commands.whenToUse: When you only want to temporarily hide one file’s changes.
commands.tip: Keeps other changes untouched.

commands.title: Git garbage collection
commands.description: Cleans and optimizes Git repository storage.
commands.howToUse: Run inside repository when maintenance is needed.
commands.whenToUse: When repo becomes large or slow over time.
commands.tip: Helps improve Git performance.

commands.title: Verify repository integrity
commands.description: Checks repository for corruption or missing objects.
commands.howToUse: Run to verify repository health.
commands.whenToUse: When debugging Git issues or after recovery operations.
commands.tip: Use before serious maintenance operations.

commands.title: Check why a file is ignored
commands.description: Shows why a file is ignored by Git.
commands.howToUse: Replace filename with target file.
commands.whenToUse: When Git ignores a file unexpectedly.
commands.tip: Helps debug .gitignore rules.

commands.title: Create status alias
commands.description: Creates a shortcut for git status.
commands.howToUse: Run once globally.
commands.whenToUse: When optimizing Git workflow speed.
commands.tip: Use 'git st' instead of 'git status'.

commands.title: Create pretty log alias
commands.description: Creates a visual Git log shortcut.
commands.howToUse: Run once globally.
commands.whenToUse: When viewing commit history in a graph format.
commands.tip: Makes Git history easier to understand.

commands.title: Show files changed in last commit
commands.description: Displays files modified in the latest commit.
commands.howToUse: Run inside repository.
commands.whenToUse: When reviewing the last commit.
commands.tip: Quick audit of recent changes.

commands.title: Recover a deleted branch
commands.code: git reflog && git branch recovered-branch abc1234
commands.description: Restores a deleted branch using reflog history.
commands.howToUse: Find commit hash in reflog and recreate branch.
commands.whenToUse: When a branch was accidentally deleted.
commands.tip: Reflog is your safety net in Git.

commands.title: Remove file from all history
commands.description: Removes a file from all commits in repository history.
commands.howToUse: Replace file path and run carefully inside repository.
commands.whenToUse: When sensitive data like API keys were committed.
commands.tip: This rewrites history and should be used with caution.
